A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same PARC/PERL study. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v4 reports original premise-identification and error-classification experiments on PERL, with results in Tables 1–5 and appendix Tables 6–10.

after.justification: v5 retains the original PERL experiments and adds ProcessBench evaluations in Section 5.3 and Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: Section 3, Algorithm 1, and the appendix prompts retain the same premise extraction, mathematical and logical verification, and accumulation-error detection procedures. ProcessBench applies the existing strategy to another evaluation task without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v5 adds human-annotated ProcessBench solutions from its GSM8K and MATH splits, testing first-incorrect-step localization. This extends evaluation beyond PERL while remaining within mathematical reasoning and retaining all four existing PERL sources.

E2.justification: The PERL comparators remain unchanged. ProcessBench Tables 6–7 introduce comparison with Zheng et al.'s whole-solution critic, which identifies the first erroneous step, distinct from the existing Full Context baseline that classifies individual steps.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds binary first-error evaluation that excludes subsequent steps and reports Correct, Wrong, F1, and Delta, alongside the retained PERL error-type accuracy protocol. Appendix A.2 also revises the stated graph-summary population from 1,370 to 607 PARCs; this reporting correction does not establish resampling or reruns.

E4.justification: The aggregative-versus-dyadic comparison, oracle-versus-model premises ablation, error-type analysis, synthetic-versus-natural error comparison, and Figure 2 case study are retained. ProcessBench adds benchmark results, without a separate new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing annotation audit and temperature-zero disclosure are unchanged, and the new ProcessBench tables retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All retained result tables match, but v5 adds substantial external first-error evaluation evidence in Tables 6–7. For example, ProcessBench MATH F1 is 35.9 for the Qwen 2.5 32B baseline versus 66.5 for PARC; GSM8K instead shows declines from 47.2 to 47.0 for Qwen 2.5 7B and 75.6 to 74.1 for 72B. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v4 scores.

T1.justification: The premise definitions, verifiability and minimality conditions, mathematical expressions, and complexity discussion are retained. Changing the reasoning-chain symbol from R to r in Section 3.1 is a notation correction, with no new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about premise identification, improved error detection, accumulation errors, and PERL. ProcessBench supplies additional supporting evidence without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly interprets ProcessBench as confirming the PERL findings and describes its first-error-only boundary. Its assertion of 'consistent gains' overlooks the two GSM8K F1 declines in Table 6; existing interpretations and caveats elsewhere remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a footnote stating that code and data are available at a repository address, whereas v4 only promises a future PERL release. The PDFs establish this added access disclosure; serving software, model variants, temperature, and appendix prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive related-work contrasts are retained. ProcessBench and Zheng et al. (2024) already appear in v4, including the contrast concerning first-error-only annotation; their new experimental use does not revise the original novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v5 adds Section 5.3, makes limited wording and terminology corrections, aligns the running header with the title, corrects an author-name diacritic, and places Acknowledgments before the unnumbered Impact Statement. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds two compact ProcessBench tables and reflows existing tables and appendix material. Appendix Tables 6–16 become Tables 8–18; Figures 1–2 and the retained table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: ProcessBench adds useful validation against human annotations beyond the model-annotated PERL dataset. The access disclosure and correction of the inconsistent PARC count also improve documentation. These gains are limited by first-error-only coverage and the overstated 'consistent gains' interpretation despite two GSM8K declines, supporting a modest overall improvement.
